entries.desc: Grass on top of soil. Break it and you get Dirt.
Soil: tiny bits of rock mixed with old plant matter.
Plain rock. Most of the underground is stone.
A dark rock that splits into flat sheets.
Coal formed from plants in ancient forests and marshes. They were buried and squeezed for millions of years.
entries.fact: Coal is a rock rich in carbon. Some coal is over 300 million years old. Some is much younger.

entries.desc: Sand is mostly tiny grains of quartz. Bake 2 in the Oven for Glass.
entries.fact: Glass makers melt sand with soda ash and limestone at about 1,500 °C.

entries.desc: Small rounded stones, often found in river beds.
Baked clay bricks. Strong when you push on them.
Stone cut into bricks.
Boards sawn from a log. 1 Log makes 4.
A piece of tree trunk. The rings show its age.
entries.fact: Where winters are cold, a tree adds one ring each year. Count the rings to find its age.

entries.desc: Leaves make food for the tree from sunlight. Sometimes a Berry falls out.
entries.fact: Leaves use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make sugar (photosynthesis).

entries.desc: A soft block of dyed cloth.
A soft block of dyed cloth.
A soft block of dyed cloth.
A soft block of undyed cloth.
Frozen water crystals. Lands soft.
entries.fact: Snow crystals have six sides or six arms. That comes from how water molecules link up. Most real snowflakes are lopsided.

entries.desc: Frozen water. In Bertopia it does not slide.
entries.fact: Ice floats because water expands when it freezes.

entries.desc: Sand stained red by iron. Bake it for Red Brick.
Sand melted and cooled until you can see through it.
entries.fact: Glass is a solid, but its atoms are jumbled. They are not lined up in a neat crystal pattern.

entries.desc: The floor of the world at y -64. It never breaks.
A table for making things from wood, cloth and stone.
entries.inside: A lever arm and a firm table let your hands push harder and cut straighter.

entries.desc: Bakes food and turns sand into glass.
entries.inside: Heat makes dough rise and bake. Much hotter heat melts sand into glass.

entries.desc: Sells your goods to townsfolk while you play.
entries.inside: A coin slot checks size and weight to tell coins apart.

entries.desc: The town store. Restock things you have already found.
Tap it to set your home spot.
entries.inside: Sleep lets your body and brain rest and repair.

entries.desc: Holds 18 stacks. Two side by side make a Double Box.
entries.inside: A box is a frame that spreads weight into its corners.

entries.desc: A grass whose seeds are ground into flour.
A tall plant that grows by water. Here it gives sugar.
A door made from 6 Planks. Tap to open.
An open wood door.
A door with glass panes. Tap to open.
An open glass door.
A steel door. Only a button, lever or power opens it.
An open metal door.
Slides open when powered and someone walks up.
An open sliding door.
Flip it to turn a circuit on or off.
entries.inside: A switch closes a gap in a circuit so power can flow.

entries.desc: A lever switched on.
entries.inside: A switch closes a gap in a circuit so power can flow.

entries.desc: Press it for 1.5 seconds of power.
entries.inside: A spring pushes the button back, so the circuit opens again.

entries.desc: A pressed button.
entries.inside: A spring pushes the button back, so the circuit opens again.

entries.desc: Melts ore into metal. Its Forge tab shapes the metal.
entries.inside: Heat melts metal from rock. Carbon from coal pulls oxygen away from the metal.

entries.desc: Builds anything with a battery, silicon or a chip. Runs on charge.
entries.inside: Small motors move a tool along three directions to build a part step by step.

entries.desc: Rusty rock full of iron. Most metal people use is iron.
entries.fact: Iron is the most-used metal on Earth. Steel is mostly iron.

entries.desc: Rock with copper in it. Copper carries electricity, so wires use it.
entries.fact: Electricity flows through copper easily. That is why wires use it.

entries.desc: Rock with zinc. Zinc coats steel so it does not rust.
entries.fact: Zinc coating (galvanizing) keeps steel from rusting.

entries.desc: A battery light. Tap for Low, Medium or High.
entries.fact: LEDs use much less energy than old light bulbs.
entries.inside: An LED turns electricity into light. It wastes much less energy as heat than an old bulb.

entries.desc: Like a wall outlet: it always gives power.
entries.fact: A wall outlet in the U.S. gives about 120 volts.
entries.inside: A charger pushes electricity back into a battery to refill its stored energy.

entries.desc: A tiny glow. A little chemical makes a short light.
entries.inside: Two chemicals react and give off energy as light, with almost no heat.

entries.desc: A chemical light. Once it is used up, it is done.
entries.fact: A glow stick glows when two chemicals mix: chemiluminescence.
entries.inside: Bending the stick breaks a glass tube inside, so two chemicals mix and glow.

entries.desc: A big glow stick. A dye takes the energy and picks the color.
entries.inside: The dye takes the energy from the reaction and gives it off as its own color.

entries.desc: Cold slows the reaction, so it glows longer.
entries.fact: Cold slows chemical reactions, so a cold glow stick lasts longer.
entries.inside: Cold makes molecules move slower, so the reaction is slower and lasts longer.

entries.desc: A cave moss that glows. Glowing fungi are real. No real moss makes its own light, so this is a Bertopia idea.
entries.fact: Some real fungi make their own light. People call it foxfire. Scientists call it bioluminescence (living light).

entries.desc: Corn is a grain. Some plastics are made from corn.
Turns sunlight into power. Its cell runs 2 strips through the night.
entries.fact: Most solar cells are made from silicon.
entries.inside: Sunlight knocks electrons loose in silicon. The loose electrons flow as electricity.

entries.desc: A thin light that uses 1 charge a minute.
entries.inside: Many small LEDs in a row share one wire, so one strip lights a long line.

entries.desc: Carries power from makers to users. Glows teal when powered.
entries.inside: Electrons move easily through copper, so it carries power with little loss.

entries.desc: In Bertopia water stays still and never floods a build.
entries.fact: Water is H2O: two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

entries.desc: Dark crystals of cassiterite, the main tin ore. About 9 parts copper to 1 part tin makes bronze.
entries.fact: Bronze is copper plus tin. A whole time in history is named after it: the Bronze Age.

entries.desc: White crystals of silica, the same stuff as most sand.
entries.fact: Quartz is silicon + oxygen (SiO2). Most sand is quartz.

entries.desc: Dune sand with quartz grains you can collect.
Soft, sticky earth found by water. Bake it into Brick.
entries.fact: Clay is made of tiny flat mineral grains. Fired clay becomes brick.

entries.desc: A thin gray stripe of clay. It is left from a space rock that hit long ago.
entries.fact: Earth has a thin clay layer found all over the world. It is rich in iridium. That is a clue that a giant asteroid hit Earth about 66 million years ago.

entries.desc: No metal reflects light better than silver.
entries.fact: Silver carries electricity best of all metals. Copper is close, and it costs much less.

entries.desc: Gold is found in quartz veins in hard rock, and as flakes in river gravel.
entries.fact: Gold never rusts, so very old gold objects still shine.

entries.desc: Soft, shiny carbon. It formed when heat and pressure changed rocks that held old plant and animal remains.
entries.fact: Pencil "lead" is really graphite mixed with clay.

entries.desc: Gravel you already panned. It has nothing left to find.
Metal so hot it flows. Here it bounces you back to safety.
Salt left behind where an old lake dried up.
entries.fact: Table salt is sodium chloride (NaCl).

entries.desc: Beach sand rich in heavy, dark minerals. Some of them hold titanium.
entries.fact: Many black sands get their color from heavy minerals like magnetite and ilmenite.

entries.desc: Red-brown earth rich in aluminum. It forms where rock weathers in warm, wet places.
entries.fact: Almost all aluminum comes from bauxite.

entries.desc: A heavy black mineral. It holds titanium.
entries.fact: Ilmenite is the main ore of titanium.

entries.desc: One of the rarest metals in the crust. Only deep under Emberdeep.
entries.fact: Platinum is used in car parts that clean exhaust.

entries.desc: Dark rock made when lava cools.
entries.fact: Most of the ocean floor is basalt.

entries.desc: Soil with a cap of snow.
Cotton fluff is plant fiber. 3 Cotton spin into 1 Cloth.
Flowers feed bees and butterflies. 1 Flower makes 2 Paint dabs.
Sun dries seawater. The salt stays behind.
entries.inside: The Sun heats the water until it evaporates. The salt cannot evaporate, so it stays.

entries.desc: Holds 3 things and shows all 3.
entries.inside: Brackets carry the shelf weight into the wall.

entries.desc: Holds 4 things and shows all 4.
entries.inside: Each board holds weight across its supports, like a small bridge.

entries.desc: A table with 1 drawer: 6 slots.
entries.inside: A drawer slides on rails, so it moves smoothly in and out.

entries.desc: 2 drawers, 12 slots, 1 thing on top.
entries.inside: Drawers slide on rails, so they move smoothly in and out.

entries.desc: 24 slots behind a door you can lock.
entries.inside: A lock uses pins that only line up with the right key.

entries.desc: 24 slots, lockable, shows its top 4 things.
entries.inside: Glass lets light through, so you can see inside without opening it.

entries.desc: 36 slots in steel, lockable.
entries.inside: Steel is strong and hard to bend, which protects what is inside.

entries.desc: A label for a Box or a path.
A clear tube that moves items 2 blocks a second.
entries.fact: Factories use conveyors to move goods from step to step.
entries.inside: A gentle push of air moves light things along a tube.

entries.desc: A tube with copper rings: 6 blocks a second.
entries.inside: Copper coils make a magnetic push that speeds items along.

entries.desc: Only lets in items that match its rule.
entries.inside: A sensor reads each item and opens a gate only for a match.

entries.desc: Pulls a stack out of storage every 2 seconds.
entries.inside: A small motor and arm pull one stack at a time on a timer.

entries.desc: Sends items down up to 4 outputs by rule.
entries.fact: Recycling centers sort materials by type.
entries.inside: A sensor reads each item and flips a gate to send it the right way.

entries.desc: Links storage into one network.
entries.inside: A cable carries signals as tiny changes in electricity.

entries.desc: The brain of a storage network. 1 per player.
entries.inside: A computer keeps a list of where every item is stored.

entries.desc: Holds 4 Drives.
entries.inside: A drive stores information as tiny switches set to on or off.

entries.desc: A search engine for your stuff.
entries.fact: A search engine finds things by looking through an index.
entries.inside: A search looks through an index, like the index at the back of a book.

entries.desc: Snaps onto a Box so the network can see inside.
entries.inside: A sensor counts what is in the box and reports it to the network.

entries.desc: Sends items (never people) to its partner pad.
entries.fact: Real teleporting is not possible. Scientists can only send tiny bits of data from one particle to another.
entries.inside: In Bertopia items jump between pads. Real teleporting of objects is not possible.

entries.desc: Charges your Delivery Drone and sends it off.
entries.inside: Contacts on the pad touch the drone and refill its battery.

entries.desc: Stores 40 charges for the night.
entries.inside: Batteries store energy as chemicals and give it back as electricity.

entries.desc: A teleport pad that talks to your network.
entries.inside: In Bertopia it links the pads to your network. Real teleporting of objects is not possible.

entries.desc: A spring pad. It stores energy when you land and gives it back.
entries.fact: A spring stores energy when squashed and gives it back.

entries.desc: Lights up where you step. Smooth fades, never strobe.
Tap to raise the pitch. The block under it picks the instrument.
entries.fact: A higher pitch means the sound wave vibrates faster.
entries.inside: Tapping makes the block vibrate. Faster vibrations make a higher pitch.

entries.desc: An 8-pad keyboard you can play.
entries.inside: Each pad plays a different pitch. Higher pads vibrate faster.

entries.desc: An 8-pad drum kit.
entries.inside: A drum skin vibrates when hit. A tighter skin makes a higher sound.

entries.desc: An 8-pad guitar.
entries.inside: A string vibrates when plucked. A shorter or tighter string sounds higher.

entries.desc: Plays Music Discs, including your own DJ Berty songs.
entries.inside: A speaker cone moves back and forth to push air and make sound waves.

entries.desc: A squash that ripens in autumn.
entries.fact: Pumpkins are fruit, because they hold seeds.

entries.desc: A carved pumpkin with an LED inside, never a flame.
Dried corn stalks tied in a bundle.
Autumn leaves raked into a pile.
A wooden crate of autumn apples.
A soft, smiling ghost-shaped LED light.
A fake cobweb. It is just for looks.
Bright orange flowers that bloom from summer into autumn.
Bright paper banners with cut-out shapes.
A tile with a bright marigold flower pattern.
entries.artStatus: redraw: marigold flowers only, no skull shapes

entries.desc: A floor tile with a simple geometric pattern. Paint it any color.
A strand of small LED lights.
Where Wonder Lab gadgets and effects are made.
entries.inside: Scientists test one change at a time so they know what caused a result.

entries.desc: A player-size pad you can warp to with a Warp Key.
entries.inside: In Bertopia a Warp Key brings you here. Real teleporting of people is not possible.

entries.desc: Tap to set where you come back.
entries.inside: Trapped air inside the bag slows heat loss and keeps you warm.

entries.desc: A shared spawn spot for your crew.
entries.inside: A banner is a flag that helps a team find its meeting spot.

entries.desc: Marks a play zone for Hide-and-Seek and mini-games.
entries.inside: A boundary marks the edges so everyone knows where the game is.

entries.desc: Teacher-flag door to the Build world.
Read Blueprint Scrolls here to unlock new materials.
entries.inside: A drawing with exact measurements lets anyone build the same thing.

entries.desc: A bench with no dust. You make the finest parts here.
entries.inside: Filters take dust out of the air. Dust can ruin tiny electronic parts.

entries.desc: A solid block of copper.
A solid block of steel.
Polished silver behind glass reflects light.
A trophy for filling half the Bertodex.
Shows the trophies you earned.
A light, hollow grass stem. Strong for its weight.
Thin wood layers glued with the grain crossing.
Stone cut into neat blocks.
A hollow concrete block, like real building blocks.
Strong when pushed, cracks when pulled.
Overlapping tiles shed rain.
Darker glass. It lets less light through, but you can still see through it.
Lets light through but blurs what is behind it.
A thin sheet of glass.
A cluster of quartz crystals.
Holds what did not fit. Take-only, never deleted.
A plaque cast in bronze.
Speckled rock made from slowly cooled magma.
entries.fact: Granite cooled slowly underground, so its crystals grew big enough to see.

entries.desc: Soil weathered for a long time in a warm, wet climate.
A tree with pale bark.
Light green leaves.
A tree that keeps its needles all winter.
Needle leaves that shed snow.
Flowers feed bees and butterflies.
Flowers feed bees and butterflies.
Still seawater. A Salt Pan beside it makes salt.
Dried grass pressed into a bale, used to feed animals.
entries.fact: Hay is grass that is cut and dried so animals can eat it in winter.

entries.desc: Gourds are cousins of pumpkins and squash, in many shapes.
entries.fact: Gourds have hard shells and were used as bowls and bottles long ago.

entries.desc: A straw figure farmers use to keep birds off crops.
Paper bats. Real bats eat lots of insects at night.
entries.fact: One bat can eat hundreds of insects in one night.

entries.desc: A pumpkin with a face you carved yourself. An LED inside makes it glow.
A wooden sign with a bat cut-out. Write a friendly message on it.
A hanging lantern with an LED glow, never a flame.
A seat for a table. Use it to sit; move to get up.
A seat with no back. Use it to sit; move to get up.
A long seat for 2. Use it to sit; move to get up.
A table. Put chairs, stools or a bench next to it.
LED string lights. Steady, or a slow twinkle when Motion is on. Never flashes.
entries.fact: LED string lights use far less power than old bulbs.

entries.desc: A ring of evergreen branches.
A wrapped box for decoration. It holds nothing.
A friendly snow figure. It never melts here.
A tile with shiny round ornaments.
A red and white striped block.
A plain string of blue and soft-white LED bulbs.
entries.origin: Blue and white lights are hung for Hanukkah in many Jewish homes.

entries.desc: A flat mat woven in red, black and green.
entries.origin: Woven mats (mkeka) are laid out for Kwanzaa in many African American homes.

entries.desc: A basket of fruit and corn.
entries.origin: Fruit and corn are set out for Kwanzaa and at many harvest festivals.

entries.desc: A round red paper lantern with a steady LED glow.
entries.origin: Red paper lanterns are hung for Lunar New Year in many East Asian homes.

entries.desc: A long, friendly paper dragon with a steady LED glow.
entries.origin: Paper dragons are carried in Lunar New Year parades.

entries.desc: A metal-and-glass lantern with geometric windows and an LED glow.
entries.origin: Fanous lanterns light streets during Ramadan in Egypt and nearby countries.

entries.desc: A block covered in bright paint splats.
entries.origin: People throw colored powder at Holi, a spring festival from India.

entries.desc: A dish of sprouted green grass.
entries.origin: Sprouted greens (sabzeh) are grown for Nowruz, the new year in Afghanistan, Iran and nearby countries.

entries.desc: A paper heart with flowers on it.
entries.origin: Hearts are shared during Kindness Week.

entries.desc: A flower that charges by day and glows softly at night.
entries.origin: Solar Flowers celebrate Earth Day and clean energy.

entries.desc: A tile with black, white and red zigzags.
entries.origin: Imigongo is zigzag art from eastern Rwanda.

entries.desc: A tile painted with bright flower sprays.
entries.origin: Petrykivka is a Ukrainian folk style of flower painting.

entries.desc: A tall woven basket with a lid.
entries.origin: A mesob is a woven table-basket from Eritrea and Ethiopia.

entries.desc: Plant it on grass or dirt. It grows into a tree.
entries.fact: A sapling is a young tree.

entries.desc: Breaks stone. Wears out after 60 breaks and leaves a stick.
Mines 3× faster than a hand.
Mines 4× faster than a hand.
Mines 6× faster than a hand.
2 Planks make 4 Sticks.
A wooden pan. Swirl river gravel to find heavy gold flakes.
entries.fact: Gold is much heavier than sand of the same size. In a swirling pan, gold sinks and water washes the sand away.

entries.desc: Scoops 1 block of still water.
Places 1 block of still water.
A small fruit. Leaves sometimes drop one.
Ground wheat seeds.
Sweet crystals from plant juice.
Flour, sugar and berries, baked.
Baked flour.
The first paints were made from colored earth called ochre. The color comes from pigments.
entries.fact: Pigments give paint its color. Early paints used colored earth, charcoal and plants.

entries.desc: Corn kernels. Cook 2 in the Oven for Bioplastic.
entries.fact: Corn is a grass. Each kernel is a seed.

entries.desc: Plant it on Dirt or Grass.
Some plastics are made from plants, like corn.
entries.fact: Some plastics are made from corn starch instead of oil.

entries.desc: A clear tube for glow sticks and machines.
The two chemicals of a glow stick, ready to react.
Takes the reaction energy and glows. The dye picks the color.
A small glass bottle. 1 Glass makes 2.
Copper straight from the rock. Smelt it into an ingot.
Crushed copper. 1 Raw Copper makes 2.
Smelted copper. 1 makes 4 Copper Wire.
Thin copper wire. It carries power.
entries.fact: Almost every building has copper wires inside. They carry power to lights and plugs.

entries.desc: Smelted iron, ready to become steel.
Iron with a little carbon. Springs back until pushed too far.
entries.fact: Steel is iron with a small amount of carbon, which makes it much stronger.

entries.desc: Smelted zinc.
Smelted tin.
About 9 parts copper to 1 part tin, like real tin bronze.
entries.fact: Bronze is about 90% copper and 10% tin.

entries.desc: Silver, smelted and ready to use.
A tiny flake from a river. 9 make a Gold Nugget.
entries.fact: Gold is very heavy for its size. So it sinks to the bottom of a pan.

entries.desc: A lump of gold.
Smelted gold.
Gold beaten very thin. 1 Ingot makes 16.
A clear crystal made of silicon and oxygen.
Sand and quartz are silica. Heating them with carbon pulls out silicon.
entries.fact: Computer chips are made from silicon.

entries.desc: A tiny silicon circuit.
entries.fact: A chip holds millions or billions of tiny switches called transistors.

entries.desc: Put copper and zinc in a sour or salty liquid. That makes a simple battery.
entries.fact: A battery stores energy in chemicals. When you use it, the chemicals make power.

entries.desc: Steel coiled so it springs back.
Steel wires twisted together. Very strong when pulled, but floppy when pushed.
An I-shaped steel beam.
A wooden beam. 2 Planks make 1.
Plant fiber. 3 make 1 Cloth.
entries.fact: Cotton fibers grow around the seeds of the cotton plant.

entries.desc: Plant it on Dirt or Grass.
Cloth woven from cotton.
Sodium chloride: the salt on food.
A grain of platinum from an Emberdeep river.
A lump of platinum.
Platinum melts at 1,768 °C, so it needs the Embercore upgrade.
White powder made from bauxite. It takes a lot of power to make it into aluminum.
A light metal. It is common, but making it takes lots of electricity.
In Bertopia it does a Steel Beam's job. Real aluminum is about a third as heavy as steel, but it bends more.
White powder refined from black sand.
Titanium is not rare. It is hard to refine.
Soft carbon flakes.
One of the rarest metals. It stays shiny because air and water barely change it.
The rarest find of all. For its size, iridium is one of the two heaviest elements.
Free colors, looks only.
+6 slots.
+12 slots.
+18 slots. Max carry 33.
The fob sends a radio signal; the bot follows the strongest signal.
A little bot that follows you and carries your stuff.
8 kinds, 512 items.
32 kinds, 2,048 items.
64 kinds, 8,192 items.
Slow, cheap and visible. Carries 4 stacks.
entries.fact: Delivery drones balance speed, battery life and how much they carry.

entries.desc: A rock has no motor. That is why it is so slow.
Gravity pulls everything down. The hat pushes back a little, for a little while.
Plays a song in a Jukebox.
Warps you to your own Warp Pad.
Basic first aid.
A plant drink for resting up.
First aid for you and your crew.
Calls your Pet Rock and Bot.
Releases friendly critters for a while.
Mimicry: copy the look of a block or critter.
Camouflage: match the background.
Magnets pull iron and steel.
A floating light orb.
A gas plus a liquid makes foam.
Freezes still water so you can walk on it.
Remote-powers your own circuit for a few seconds.
Read it at the Drafting Table. It unlocks a new material.
The everyday coin.
A rarer coin.
A rare coin.
A very rare coin.
The rarest coin of all.
1 Flower makes 2 Paint dabs.
entries.fact: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower.

entries.desc: An autumn fruit.
A safe scoop, not a knife. Use it on a Pumpkin to carve a face.
A little bot that follows you and carries your stuff.
Flies 3 blocks above the tallest block on its route.
A rock has no motor. That is why it is so slow.
A beetle that makes its own light.
Visits flowers for nectar.
Sings to talk to other birds.
Jumps far with long back legs.
Digs burrows with many rooms.
Can twist in the air to land on its feet.
Grass, oak trees and the town. Coal, clay, iron and a little copper.
Pale granite hills with quartz crystals. Look for tin and gold veins.
A flat dry lake bed with white salt crust. Iron, silver and zinc in the hills.
Beaches, cliffs and the sea. Black sand and the Salt Pan.
Snowy mountains and frozen lakes. Look for ice and tin.
Dark basalt hills. Copper at the edges, platinum deep down.
Still seawater at the edge of Tidewell.
Bertyville: the store, the stations and everyone's plots.
Takes you to your own Warp Pad.
Fixes hearts when Damage is on.
Calls your Pet Rock or Bot, or lets friendly critters out.
Look like a block or critter for a while.
Blend into the background.
A game mode that uses Morph, Camo and Tag.
Science that looks like magic: magnets, light, foam, frost and sparks.
Float gently for 10 seconds.
